drivingQuestion: Does an item whose absorbed forbidden substance could be wrung out remain forbidden, so that the piece which absorbed the milk itself becomes non-kosher and forbids the rest of the pot?
outcomeNote: The sugya establishes that Rav holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור and that the tannaitic dispute of R' Yehuda and the Rabbis turns on that same question; Rav Aḥa of Difti's alternative account is rejected by Ravina from the wording of Rabbi's ruling, and the unit closes with ותו לא מידי.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טַעְמוֹ וְלֹא מַמָּשׁוֹ בְּעָלְמָא – דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Abaye said:» The principle that «the flavor» of a forbidden food renders prohibited the substance in which it is absorbed, «and» it is «not» necessary for there to be «actual» forbidden substance, applies «by Torah law in general,» and not just to the prohibition of meat cooked in milk.

segments.he: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּרַבָּנַן, מִבָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב מַאי טַעְמָא לָא גָּמְרִינַן? דְּחִדּוּשׁ הוּא. אִי חִדּוּשׁ הוּא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא נוֹתֵן טַעַם נָמֵי!
segments.en: «As, if it enters your mind» that the principle applies to other prohibited foods «by rabbinic law,» one can claim: «What is the reason» that «we do not learn» that it applies by Torah law «from» the analogous case of «meat» cooked «in milk?» It must be «because» the prohibition of meat cooked in milk «is a novelty» that is not derived through logical reasoning, as each substance is separately permitted, and they are prohibited only when cooked together. No analogies can be drawn to a novelty. But «if» the prohibition «is a novelty,» then «even if there is not» enough milk to «impart flavor,» the meat and milk should «also» be prohibited. Since the measure of the prohibition follows the standard principles of mixtures, the prohibition itself is apparently not a novelty. One may therefore draw an analogy to other mixtures, inferring that this measure applies to them by Torah law as well.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: דֶּרֶךְ בִּשּׁוּל אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה.
segments.en: «Rava said to» Abaye: This is not a valid proof. The prohibition of meat cooked in milk is in fact a novelty and differs from other prohibited mixtures. Nevertheless, its measure is the imparting of flavor only because the action «the Torah prohibited» is in «the manner of cooking,» and cooking involves the imparting of flavor.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן טַעַם בַּחֲתִיכָה, חֲתִיכָה עַצְמָהּ נַעֲשֵׂית נְבֵלָה, וְאוֹסֶרֶת כׇּל הַחֲתִיכוֹת כּוּלָּן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מִינָהּ.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if the piece of meat acquires the flavor of milk, it is forbidden. «Rav says: Once» the milk «imparts flavor to the piece» of meat, the «piece itself becomes non-kosher» meat in its own right. «And» therefore, if one did not immediately remove the piece from the pot, «it renders all the pieces» of meat in the pot «forbidden,» even if they are together more than sixty times the size of that forbidden piece. This is «because they are» the same «type» as the forbidden piece, and as a rule, a substance in contact with the same type of substance cannot be nullified.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא: מִכְּדֵי רַב כְּמַאן אָמַר לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ? כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר מִין בְּמִינוֹ לֹא בָּטֵיל, לֵימָא פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרָבָא?
segments.en: «Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina: Now» consider, «in accordance with whose» opinion did «Rav say his halakha?» It is «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, who said» that «a type» of food mixed with food «of» its «own type is not nullified.» If so, «shall we say» that Rav «disagrees with Rava’s» interpretation of Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion?

segments.he: דְּאָמַר רָבָא: קָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כׇּל שֶׁהוּא מִין וּמִינוֹ וְדָבָר אַחֵר – סַלֵּק אֶת מִינוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ רָבֶה עָלָיו וּמְבַטְּלוֹ.
segments.en: «As Rava said: Rabbi Yehuda holds» with regard to «any» tripartite mixture «consisting of» a forbidden «type» of food, a permitted food of «the same type, and another» food «item» that is permitted, one «disregards» the permitted food that is its «own type as though it were not there, and» if the permitted food «that is not» of «its own type is more than» the forbidden food, the permitted food «nullifies» the forbidden food. In the case Rav describes, although the other pieces of meat are of the same type as the piece that has become forbidden, the gravy in the pot is not of the same type, and it should nullify the forbidden piece. Since Rav does not mention this principle, he apparently disagrees with it.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי דִּנְפַל בְּרוֹטֶב רַכָּה – הָכִי נָמֵי, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן – דִּנְפַל בְּרוֹטֶב עָבָה.
segments.en: Ravina «said to him: If» the forbidden substance «fell into thin gravy,» Rav would concede that the gravy would «indeed» nullify the piece of meat, since the two substances are of different types. «But here we are dealing with» a case «where it fell into thick gravy,» which is composed of meat residue. Since the gravy is of the same substance as the meat, the forbidden piece is not nullified.

segments.he: וּמַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ מוּתָּר, חֲתִיכָה אַמַּאי נַעֲשֵׂית נְבֵלָה? אֶלָּא קָסָבַר אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר.
segments.en: The Gemara returns to Rav’s statement that the piece of meat upon which the milk fell is considered a non-kosher item in its own right. «And what does» Rav «maintain» in this regard? «If he maintains» that an item «that can be wrung» to remove the forbidden substance it contains becomes «permitted» again after wringing, then it follows that only the absorbed substance is truly forbidden. If so, «why» should this «piece» of meat itself «become non-kosher?» Once it has been mixed into the stew, the milk it has absorbed should be evenly distributed throughout the pot and be nullified. «Rather,» Rav must «maintain» that even an item «that can be wrung» to remove the forbidden substance is «forbidden.»

segments.he: דְּאִיתְּמַר: רַב וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמְרִי: אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ – אָסוּר, שְׁמוּאֵל וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי: אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ – מוּתָּר.
segments.en: The Gemara elaborates: «As it was stated: Rav and Rabbi Ḥanina and Rabbi Yoḥanan say» that even an item «that can be wrung» to remove the forbidden substance is «forbidden,» whereas «Shmuel, and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi, «and Reish Lakish say:» An item «that can be wrung» to remove the forbidden substance is «permitted.»

segments.he: וְסָבַר רַב אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר? וְהָאִיתְּמַר: כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ יוֹרָה שֶׁל חָלָב, אָמַר רַב: בָּשָׂר אָסוּר וְחָלָב מוּתָּר, וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר,
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And does Rav» really «maintain» that an item «that can be wrung» to remove the forbidden substance is «forbidden? But wasn’t it stated:» If «an olive-bulk of meat fell into a pot of milk» so large that the meat did not impart flavor to it, «Rav says:» The «meat is forbidden,» as it absorbed the taste of the milk, «but» the «milk is permitted,» since it did not absorb the taste of the meat. «But if it enters your mind» that according to Rav an item «that can be wrung is forbidden,»

segments.he: חָלָב אַמַּאי מוּתָּר? חָלָב נְבֵלָה הוּא!
segments.en: «why is» the «milk permitted?» All the milk that the meat absorbed «is» rendered «non-kosher milk» in and of itself. When it seeps back out of the meat, it cannot be nullified by the rest of the milk, which is the same substance, as Rav holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda that a type of food mixed with food of its own type is not nullified. Therefore, the whole pot of milk should be prohibited.

segments.he: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַב אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר, וְשָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״לֹא תְבַשֵּׁל גְּדִי בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ – גְּדִי אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה, וְלֹא חָלָב.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Rav actually maintains» that an item «that can be wrung» to remove the forbidden substance is «prohibited, and there,» the pot of milk mentioned above «is different, as the verse states: “You shall not cook a kid in its mother’s milk”» (Deuteronomy 14:21). The verse teaches that «the Torah prohibits» only the «kid,» i.e., the meat, that was cooked in milk, «but not» the «milk» that was cooked in meat. The milk is not itself rendered non-kosher.

segments.he: וְסָבַר רַב גְּדִי אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה וְלֹא חָלָב? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר: חֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וַחֲצִי זַיִת חָלָב שֶׁבִּשְּׁלָן זֶה עִם זֶה, אָמַר רַב: לוֹקֶה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה עַל בִּשּׁוּלוֹ. וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ גְּדִי אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה וְלֹא חָלָב, אַאֲכִילָה אַמַּאי לוֹקֶה? חֲצִי שִׁיעוּר הוּא!
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «And does Rav» really «maintain» that «the Torah prohibits» only the «kid but not» the «milk» cooked with it? «But isn’t it stated:» If «half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of milk were cooked together, Rav says:» One «is flogged for consuming» the combined olive-bulk, as he has eaten a whole olive-bulk of forbidden food. «But he is not flogged for cooking» the two half olive-bulks, as he did not cook items of the minimum size. «And if» it should «enter your mind» that Rav holds that «the Torah prohibits» only the «kid but not» the «milk, why is» this individual «flogged for consuming» only half an olive-bulk of meat? «It is» only «half» the prohibited «measure.»

segments.he: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַב חָלָב נָמֵי אָסוּר, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ יוֹרָה רוֹתַחַת, דְּמִבְלָע בָּלַע, מִפְלָט לָא פָּלֵט.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav actually maintains» that «milk» cooked in meat «is also prohibited, and» the reason Rav permits the pot of milk mentioned above is that «here we are dealing with» a case «where» the olive-bulk of meat «fell into a boiling pot» of milk. In such a case the meat «absorbs» milk, but «it does not expel» it, and therefore the prohibited milk does not mix with the rest.

segments.he: סוֹף סוֹף כִּי נָיַיח, הֲדַר פָּלֵיט! כְּשֶׁקָּדַם וְסִילְּקוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «Ultimately, when» the pot «cools» from boiling, the meat «then expels» the prohibited milk. The Gemara answers: It is referring to a case «where he first removed» the meat before the pot cooled.

segments.he: גּוּפָא: חֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וַחֲצִי זַיִת חָלָב שֶׁבִּשְּׁלָן זֶה עִם זֶה, אָמַר רַב: לוֹקֶה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה עַל בִּשּׁוּלוֹ. מָה נַפְשָׁךְ? אִי מִצְטָרְפִין – אַבִּשּׁוּל נָמֵי לִילְקֵי, אִי לֹא מִצְטָרְפִין – אַאֲכִילָה נָמֵי לָא לִילְקֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara turns to «the» matter «itself» mentioned above: If «half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of milk were cooked together, Rav says:» One «is flogged for consuming» the mixture, «but he is not flogged for cooking it.» The Gemara objects: «Whichever way you» look at it, this ruling is problematic. «If» these two halves of olive-bulks «combine» to form the requisite measure, then «let him be flogged for cooking» them «as well.» And «if they do not combine,» then «let him not be flogged for» their «consumption either.»

segments.he: לְעוֹלָם לָא מִצְטָרְפִי, וּבְבָא מִיּוֹרָה גְּדוֹלָה.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Actually,» half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of milk «do not combine» to form the requisite measure, «and» when Rav says that one is flogged for consuming them, he is referring «to» a case where they «come from a large pot,» in which a sizable amount of meat and cheese had been cooked. The mixture is now considered a single prohibited entity, such that half an olive-bulk of the cheese and the meat can combine to constitute the requisite measure to be held liable for consumption.

segments.he: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אַף לוֹקֶה עַל בִּשּׁוּלוֹ, וְכֵן תָּנֵי לֵוִי בְּמַתְנִיתִין: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁלּוֹקֶה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ כָּךְ לוֹקֶה עַל בִּשּׁוּלוֹ, וּבְאֵי זֶה בִּשּׁוּל אָמְרוּ? בְּבִשּׁוּל שֶׁאֲחֵרִים אוֹכְלִין אוֹתוֹ מֵחֲמַת בִּשּׁוּלוֹ.
segments.en: «And Levi» disagrees with Rav on this matter, and «says:» Half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of milk can combine to form the requisite measure, and therefore one «is also flogged for cooking» the mixture. «And so Levi teaches in» his collection of «baraitot: Just as one is flogged for consuming it, so too he is flogged for cooking it. And for what» degree of «cooking did they say» that one is liable to be flogged? It is «for» a degree of «cooking» that produces food «that others,» gentiles, would «eat due to its cooking,» i.e., cooking that renders it fit for consumption.

segments.he: וְאֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ עַצְמוֹ – תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: טִפַּת חָלָב שֶׁנָּפְלָה עַל הַחֲתִיכָה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתְנָה טַעַם בַּחֲתִיכָה – הַחֲתִיכָה עַצְמָהּ נַעֲשֵׂת נְבֵלָה, וְאוֹסֶרֶת כׇּל הַחֲתִיכוֹת כּוּלָּן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מִינָהּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to the issue previously discussed: «And» the case of an item «that can be wrung» to remove an absorbed prohibited substance «is itself» the subject of a dispute between «tanna’im, as it is taught» in a baraita: If «a drop of milk fell onto a piece» of meat, «once it imparts flavor to the piece, the piece itself is rendered non-kosher» in its own right. «And» it therefore «renders all the» other «pieces» of meat in the pot «prohibited,» even if they combine to more than sixty times its size; this is «because they are» of «the same type,» and a type of food mixed with food of its own type is not nullified. This is «the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.»

segments.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁתִּתֵּן טַעַם בָּרוֹטֶב וּבַקֵּיפֶה וּבַחֲתִיכוֹת.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis say» that even the original piece of meat is not prohibited «unless» there is enough milk to «impart flavor» even «to the gravy and to the spices and to the» other «pieces» of meat in the pot, since the milk is assumed to diffuse from the first piece until it is evenly distributed throughout the pot.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּשֶׁלֹּא נִיעֵר וְשֶׁלֹּא כִּסָּה, וְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים בְּשֶׁנִּיעֵר וְכִסָּה.
segments.en: With regard to this dispute, «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «said: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears» to be correct in a case «where one did not stir» the contents of the pot «and where he did not cover» it, both of which would promote the diffusion of the milk throughout the pot. «And the statement of the Rabbis» appears to be correct in a case «where one stirred» the contents of the pot «and covered» it.

segments.he: מַאי ״לֹא נִיעֵר וְלֹא כִּסָּה״? אִילֵּימָא לֹא נִיעֵר כְּלָל, וְלֹא כִּסָּה כְּלָל – מִבְלָע בָּלַע, מִפְלָט לָא פָּלֵט.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What» is the meaning of the clause: Where «one did not stir» the pot «and did not cover» it? «If we say» that he «did not stir» the contents of the pot «at all and did not cover» it «at all,» in this case the piece of meat onto which the milk fell «absorbs» the drop of milk but «does not expel» it. Therefore, even according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda there is no reason to prohibit the other pieces of meat.

segments.he: וְאֶלָּא, לֹא נִיעֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף, וְלֹא כִּסָּה בַּתְּחִלָּה אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף, אַמַּאי? הָא בָּלַע וְהָא פָּלֵט!
segments.en: «And» if you say «rather» that «he did not not stir» the contents of the pot «at the beginning,» immediately after the milk fell in, «but» stirred «at the end,» afterward, «and» likewise «he did not cover» the pot «at the beginning but at the end,» one must ask: «Why» are all the pieces in the pot prohibited? The same milk that the piece «absorbs» it subsequently «expels,» and once the milk diffuses throughout the pot it should be nullified.

segments.he: קָסָבַר אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: Evidently, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi «maintains» that an item «that can be wrung» remains «prohibited.» Once the first piece of meat absorbs the milk, it is considered non-kosher in its own right, and even after the milk itself is nullified, the flavor of the forbidden meat renders the rest of the pieces prohibited. The flavor of the meat cannot be nullified by the other meat in the pot, since a substance in contact with the same type of substance is not nullified, according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

segments.he: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: כִּי נִיעֵר מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף וְכִסָּה מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף – אָסוּר, אַמַּאי? הָא לָא בָּלַע כְּלָל!
segments.en: The Gemara objects: From Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s acceptance of Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion only when one did not stir or cover the pot, one can conclude «by inference that Rabbi Yehuda» himself «maintains» that even «when one stirred» the contents of the pot continuously «from beginning to end,» i.e., before and after the drop of milk was absorbed, «or covered» the pot continuously «from beginning to end,» all the contents of the pot are «prohibited.» But «why» should this be so? The first piece of meat «did not absorb any» more milk than the others. Since the milk definitely diffused evenly through the pot immediately, it should be nullified, assuming that the pot’s contents amount to more than sixty times the milk.

segments.he: אֵימָא: לֹא נִיעֵר יָפֶה יָפֶה, וְלֹא כִּסָּה יָפֶה יָפֶה.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Say» that Rabbi Yehuda is stringent because one might «not» have «stirred thoroughly, or» he might «not» have «covered» the pot «thoroughly,» and therefore initially the milk might have been absorbed only by the first piece, rendering it prohibited. Afterward, when he does stir thoroughly, that piece of meat renders the other pieces prohibited. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi does not share this concern.

segments.he: אָמַר מָר, וְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים כְּשֶׁנִּיעֵר וְכִסָּה. מַאי ״נִיעֵר״ וּמַאי ״כִּסָּה״? אִילֵּימָא נִיעֵר בַּסּוֹף וְלֹא נִיעֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה, וְכִסָּה בַּסּוֹף וְלֹא כִּסָּה בַּתְּחִלָּה – הָאָמְרַתְּ נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּהָא! אֶלָּא נִיעֵר מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף, וְכִסָּה מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף.
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s statement: «The Master said» above: «And the statement of the Rabbis» appears correct in a case «where one stirred» the pot «and covered» it. The Gemara asks: «What» is the meaning of the term: «Stirred, and what» is the meaning of the term: «Covered? If we say» that he «stirred at the end,» after the first piece absorbed the milk, «and did not stir at the beginning,» beforehand, «and» likewise he «covered at the end and did not cover at the beginning,» one may respond: «Didn’t you» already «say» on the previous amud that «the statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears» to be correct «in this» case? «Rather,» it must be a case where he «stirred» continuously «from beginning to end or covered» the pot continuously «from beginning to end.»

segments.he: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: נִיעֵר בַּסּוֹף וְלֹא נִיעֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה, כִּסָּה בַּסּוֹף וְלֹא כִּסָּה בַּתְּחִלָּה – מוּתָּר.
segments.en: If so, one can conclude «by inference» from Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s qualified acceptance of the Rabbis’ opinion «that the Rabbis» themselves «maintain» that even when one «stirred» only «at the end and did not stir at the beginning,» and similarly if he «covered» the pot only «at the end and did not cover at the beginning,» all the contents of the pot are «permitted.» Even the first piece is permitted, as they hold that the milk it absorbed diffused out of it and throughout the pot.

segments.he: אַלְמָא קָסָבְרִי אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ מוּתָּר.
segments.en: «Evidently,» the Rabbis «maintain» that an item «that can be wrung» to remove the forbidden substance is «permitted.» This illustrates that tanna’im dispute this issue, as according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, an item that can be wrung to remove the forbidden substance is prohibited.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: מִמַּאי דִּבְאֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ פְּלִיגִי? דִּלְמָא אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר, וְהָכָא בְּמִין בְּמִינוֹ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר: מִין בְּמִינוֹ לֹא בָּטֵיל, וְרַבָּנַן לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּאָמְרִי: מִין בְּמִינוֹ בָּטֵיל!
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina: From where» is it derived «that» Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis «disagree with regard to» an item «that can be wrung? Perhaps» even if an item «can be wrung, everyone agrees» that it remains «prohibited, and here they disagree with regard to» whether «a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type» can be nullified. «And Rabbi Yehuda» conforms «to his» standard line of «reasoning, as he said» that «a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type cannot be nullified. And» likewise, «the Rabbis» conform «to their» standard line of «reasoning, as they said» that «a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type can be nullified.» This is why they maintain that all the meat in the pot is permitted.

segments.he: הַאי מַאי? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבָּנַן בְּמִין בְּמִינוֹ הָכָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לְהוּ, וּבְאֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ פְּלִיגִי – הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּהָא, וְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים בְּהָא.
segments.en: Ravina responded: «What is this» reasoning? «Granted, if you say that the Rabbis here hold in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda with regard to» the issue of «a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type, and they disagree with regard to» an item «that can be wrung, that is» why «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «says: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears» to be correct «in this» case, when one did not initially stir or cover the pot, «and the statement of the Rabbis» appears to be correct «in that» case, when one did initially stir or cover it, since the issue of when one stirred or covered the pot is relevant to the dispute, as explained above.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ: אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר, וְהָכָא בְּמִין בְּמִינוֹ קָמִיפַּלְגִי – הַאי נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְאֵין נִרְאִין מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, וְתוּ לָא מִידִּי.
segments.en: «But if you say: Everyone agrees» that an item «that can be wrung is prohibited, and here they disagree» only «with regard to a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type,» Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi should not phrase his statement as a qualified acceptance of both opinions, which seems arbitrary. Rather, «he should have» said «this:» I accept that a type of food is not nullified by a food of its own type. Therefore, «the statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears» correct where one did not stir initially, as the flavor of the prohibited first piece cannot be nullified; «but» it «does not appear» correct where one stirred immediately, since in that case, even the first piece is not prohibited, and I do not share Rabbi Yehuda’s concern that perhaps one did not stir thoroughly. «And nothing more» need be said.

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: טעמו ולא ממשו בעלמא דאורייתא
moves.summary: Abaye generalises the mishna's drop-of-milk rule: imparted flavour alone prohibits by Torah law in every prohibition

moves.cueHe: דאי סלקא דעתך דרבנן
moves.summary: proves it: were it only rabbinic, meat in milk would be a novelty, yet it is forbidden only when flavour is imparted

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא: דרך בישול אסרה תורה
moves.summary: Rava tells Abaye the proof fails: meat in milk is a novelty, but the Torah forbade the manner of cooking, which involves imparting flavour
moves.about: whether the measure of the meat-in-milk prohibition proves that flavour without substance is forbidden by Torah law generally

moves.cueHe: אמר רב: כיון שנתן טעם בחתיכה, חתיכה עצמה נעשית נבלה
moves.summary: Rav rules that the piece which absorbed the milk becomes non-kosher itself and forbids all the pieces as its own type

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי לרבינא: מכדי רב כמאן אמר לשמעתיה
moves.summary: asks Ravina whose tannaitic view Rav follows, and answers: R' Yehuda, who holds a type is not nullified by its own type
moves.about: in accordance with whose tannaitic opinion Rav stated his ruling that the piece itself becomes non-kosher

moves.cueHe: לימא פליגא אדרבא
moves.summary: proposes that Rav thereby contradicts Rava's account of R' Yehuda, on which a third substance nullifies the forbidden piece
moves.about: R' Yehuda's principle that a type is not nullified by its own type

moves.cueHe: דאמר רבא: קסבר רבי יהודה
moves.summary: cites Rava: R' Yehuda disregards the same type and lets the other substance nullify the prohibition
moves.about: Rava's account of how R' Yehuda treats a tripartite mixture

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אי דנפל ברוטב רכה – הכי נמי
moves.summary: Ravina answers that Rav speaks of thick gravy, which is itself of the meat's type, so nothing nullifies it
moves.about: whether Rav's ruling conflicts with Rava's account of R' Yehuda

moves.cueHe: ומאי קסבר
moves.summary: asks which premise about wringing out Rav's ruling presupposes
moves.about: which underlying premise about wringing out an absorbed prohibition Rav's ruling presupposes

moves.cueHe: אי קסבר אפשר לסוחטו מותר
moves.summary: floats that Rav holds an item which can be wrung out is permitted
moves.about: that Rav holds an item whose absorbed prohibition could be wrung out remains forbidden

moves.cueHe: חתיכה אמאי נעשית נבלה
moves.summary: knocks the float down: on that premise the piece would never become non-kosher
moves.about: the floated candidate that Rav holds an item which can be wrung out is permitted

moves.cueHe: אלא קסבר אפשר לסוחטו אסור
moves.summary: concludes that Rav holds an item which can be wrung out remains forbidden

moves.cueHe: דאיתמר
moves.summary: cites the six-sage amoraic dispute over whether an item that can be wrung out is forbidden
moves.about: the recorded amoraic dispute over whether an item that can be wrung out is forbidden

moves.cueHe: וסבר רב אפשר לסוחטו אסור? והאיתמר
moves.summary: sets against it Rav's ruling that meat which fell into a pot of milk is forbidden while the milk is permitted
moves.about: Rav's ruling that meat is forbidden but the milk permitted contradicts his holding that an item which can be wrung out is forbidden

moves.cueHe: חלב אמאי מותר
moves.summary: presses the contradiction: the absorbed milk is itself non-kosher milk and should forbid the whole pot

moves.cueHe: לעולם קסבר רב אפשר לסוחטו אסור
moves.summary: answers that meat in milk is different, and Rav's premise stands
moves.about: why Rav permits the pot of milk even though he holds that an item which can be wrung out is forbidden

moves.cueHe: דאמר קרא ״לא תבשל גדי בחלב אמו״
moves.summary: grounds the distinction in the verse: the Torah forbade the kid, not the milk
moves.about: the verse forbidding cooking a kid in its mother's milk

moves.cueHe: וסבר רב גדי אסרה תורה ולא חלב? והא איתמר
moves.summary: objects from Rav's own ruling that one is flogged for eating half an olive-bulk of each, which requires the milk to count
moves.about: Rav's ruling that one is flogged for eating half an olive-bulk of meat with half of milk contradicts the claim that the Torah forbids only the kid and not the milk

moves.cueHe: אלא, לעולם קסבר רב חלב נמי אסור
moves.summary: replaces the answer: milk too is forbidden, and the pot case is one of boiling milk, which the meat absorbs but does not expel
moves.about: why Rav permitted the pot of milk if milk cooked in meat is also forbidden

moves.cueHe: סוף סוף כי נייח, הדר פליט
moves.summary: presses that once the pot cools the meat expels the forbidden milk after all
moves.about: that the meat will expel the absorbed milk once the boiling pot cools, so the answer from a boiling pot does not hold

moves.cueHe: כשקדם וסילקו
moves.summary: answers that he removed the meat before the pot cooled
moves.about: that the case is one where the meat was removed before the pot cooled

moves.cueHe: מה נפשך
moves.summary: attacks it from both horns: if the halves combine he should be flogged for cooking too, and if not, not for eating either
moves.about: that whether or not the two half-measures combine, Rav's split ruling on eating and cooking is untenable

moves.cueHe: גופא
moves.summary: returns to Rav's half-olive-bulk ruling in its own right
moves.about: returning to Rav's ruling on half an olive-bulk of meat and half of milk in its own right

moves.cueHe: לעולם לא מצטרפי, ובבא מיורה גדולה
moves.summary: answers that they never combine, and Rav speaks of portions cut from a large pot in which full measures cooked together
moves.about: that the halves do not combine and Rav speaks of portions taken from a large pot

moves.cueHe: ולוי אמר: אף לוקה על בישולו
moves.summary: Levi rules against Rav that one is flogged for cooking the two halves as well
moves.about: whether half an olive-bulk of meat and half of milk combine so that one is flogged for cooking them as well as for eating them

moves.cueHe: וכן תני לוי במתניתין
moves.summary: cites his own baraita, which also defines the degree of cooking that incurs liability
moves.about: Levi's own baraita that one is flogged for cooking just as for eating

moves.cueHe: ואפשר לסוחטו עצמו – תנאי היא, דתניא
moves.summary: maps the amoraic dispute onto a tannaitic one and brings the baraita of the drop of milk
moves.about: the baraita of the drop of milk that fell on a piece of meat, disputed by R' Yehuda and the Rabbis

moves.cueHe: טיפת חלב שנפלה על החתיכה
moves.summary: in the baraita: the piece itself becomes non-kosher and forbids all the pieces, as they are its own type
moves.about: whether an item whose absorbed forbidden substance could be wrung out remains forbidden — the sugya maps the amoraic dispute onto this tannaitic one

moves.cueHe: וחכמים אומרים: עד שתתן טעם ברוטב ובקיפה ובחתיכות
moves.summary: the Rabbis hold nothing is forbidden unless the milk imparts flavour to gravy, spices and pieces alike
moves.about: whether a piece of meat that absorbed a drop of milk becomes forbidden in its own right, or only if the milk imparts flavour to the gravy, spices and other pieces

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי: נראין דברי רבי יהודה בשלא ניער ושלא כיסה
moves.summary: Rabbi apportions the two views: R' Yehuda where the pot was neither stirred nor covered, the Rabbis where it was
moves.about: confining R' Yehuda's ruling to a pot that was neither stirred nor covered

moves.cueHe: אילימא לא ניער כלל, ולא כיסה כלל
moves.summary: floats that he never stirred or covered at all
moves.about: the floated reading that he did not stir or cover at all, which would mean the piece absorbs but never expels

moves.cueHe: מבלע בלע, מפלט לא פלט
moves.summary: rejects it: then the piece absorbs but never expels, so even R' Yehuda would not forbid the rest

moves.cueHe: מאי ״לא ניער ולא כיסה״
moves.summary: asks what Rabbi means by 'did not stir and did not cover'
moves.about: the sense of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's phrase 'did not stir and did not cover'

moves.cueHe: ואלא, לא ניער בתחלה אלא בסוף
moves.summary: floats instead that he stirred and covered only afterwards
moves.about: why R' Yehuda forbids all the pieces if the first piece both absorbed and then expelled the milk

moves.cueHe: אמאי? הא בלע והא פלט
moves.summary: asks why all the pieces are then forbidden, since the milk absorbed was afterwards expelled and diffused

moves.cueHe: קסבר אפשר לסוחטו אסור
moves.summary: answers that Rabbi holds an item which can be wrung out stays forbidden, so the piece itself now forbids the rest
moves.about: that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi holds an item which can be wrung out remains forbidden

moves.cueHe: מכלל דרבי יהודה סבר
moves.summary: infers that R' Yehuda himself forbids even when the pot was stirred and covered throughout
moves.about: reading out of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's qualified endorsement that R' Yehuda forbids even when the pot was stirred and covered throughout

moves.cueHe: אמאי? הא לא בלע כלל
moves.summary: objects that with constant stirring the first piece absorbed nothing more than the others
moves.about: why the pieces should be forbidden when constant stirring means the first piece absorbed nothing more than the others

moves.cueHe: אימא: לא ניער יפה יפה, ולא כיסה יפה יפה
moves.summary: re-reads the clause as 'not stirred thoroughly', R' Yehuda's concern that the first piece absorbed alone
moves.about: re-reading 'did not stir and did not cover' as 'did not stir thoroughly and did not cover thoroughly'

moves.cueHe: אמר מר, ודברי חכמים כשניער וכיסה
moves.summary: re-cites Rabbi's second clause for examination
moves.about: re-citing the second clause of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's ruling in order to examine it

moves.cueHe: אילימא ניער בסוף ולא ניער בתחלה
moves.summary: floats that he stirred and covered only at the end
moves.about: settling that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's 'stirred and covered' means stirred and covered continuously from beginning to end

moves.cueHe: האמרת נראין דברי רבי יהודה בהא
moves.summary: rejects it: that case was already assigned to R' Yehuda
moves.about: the floated reading that he stirred only at the end, which Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi already assigned to R' Yehuda

moves.cueHe: אלא ניער מתחלה ועד סוף
moves.summary: settles that Rabbi means stirred and covered continuously from beginning to end

moves.cueHe: מאי ״ניער״ ומאי ״כיסה״
moves.summary: asks what 'stirred' and 'covered' mean here
moves.about: the sense of the terms 'stirred' and 'covered' in Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's second clause

moves.cueHe: מכלל דרבנן סברי
moves.summary: infers that the Rabbis permit even where he stirred only at the end, so even the first piece reverts to permitted
moves.about: reading out of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's endorsement that the Rabbis permit even when he stirred only at the end

moves.cueHe: אלמא קסברי אפשר לסוחטו מותר
moves.summary: concludes that the Rabbis hold an item which can be wrung out is permitted — hence a tannaitic dispute
moves.about: that the Rabbis hold an item whose absorbed prohibition could be wrung out is permitted

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא מדיפתי לרבינא: ממאי דבאפשר לסוחטו פליגי
moves.summary: challenges Ravina: what shows the tannaim dispute wringing out at all?
moves.about: whether the tannaitic dispute really turns on wringing out (אפשר לסוחטו) rather than on whether a type is nullified by its own type

moves.cueHe: דלמא אפשר לסוחטו דברי הכל אסור, והכא במין במינו קא מיפלגי
moves.summary: floats that all agree it is forbidden and they dispute only nullification by one's own type, each tanna following his standing view
moves.about: that R' Yehuda's ruling here follows his standing principle that a type is not nullified by its own type

moves.cueHe: האי מאי
moves.summary: Ravina dismisses the suggestion outright
moves.about: whether R' Yehuda and the Rabbis dispute wringing out or the nullification of a type by its own type

moves.cueHe: אי אמרת בשלמא דרבנן במין במינו הכא כרבי יהודה סבירא להו
moves.summary: shows his own reading accounts for Rabbi's apportioning of the two views to two cases
moves.about: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's apportioning of the two views to two cases, which only the wringing-out reading explains

moves.cueHe: אלא אי אמרת: אפשר לסוחטו דברי הכל אסור
moves.summary: on Rav Aḥa's reading Rabbi should have said 'appears correct and does not appear correct', not apportioned the views
moves.about: that on Rav Aḥa's reading Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi should have said 'the statement of R' Yehuda appears correct and does not appear correct', not apportioned the two views

moves.cueHe: ותו לא מידי
moves.summary: the suggestion is closed off: nothing more need be said

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא: דרך בישול אסרה תורה
edges.about: whether the measure of the meat-in-milk prohibition proves that flavour without substance is forbidden by Torah law generally

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי לרבינא: מכדי רב כמאן אמר לשמעתיה
edges.about: in accordance with whose tannaitic opinion Rav stated his ruling that the piece itself becomes non-kosher
